Findings:

1. (factual, BLOCKING) Several Death Toll cells do not follow the registered per-disaster value source / declared source-priority rule.

The staged metadata says the master article is universe-only and per-row values come from each per-disaster article, with master bullets only supporting universe membership. The CSV instead mixes in master-bullet or outside-source wording for central Death Toll values.

Representative source-grounding mismatches:
- Coalbrook mining disaster: staged `435`; registered per-disaster article infobox gives 437 dead and the lead repeats 437. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coalbrook_mining_disaster, infobox/lead lines 126-133.
- Senghenydd Colliery Disaster: staged `439`; registered per-disaster article says 439 miners plus one rescuer, i.e. 440 total deaths. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senghenydd_colliery_disaster, lead lines 121-123.
- Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster: staged `1 confirmed cancer death; ~2,202 disaster-related deaths from evacuation`; registered source redirects to Fukushima nuclear accident and gives 1 suspected radiation death plus at least 51 displacement-related deaths, and a page search found no `2,202` or `disaster-related` wording. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fukushima_Daiichi_nuclear_disaster, redirect/infobox/lead lines 218-248.
- Halifax Explosion: staged `Approximately 2,000`; registered per-disaster article infobox gives 1,782 confirmed deaths, and the lead says at least 1,782. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halifax_Explosion, infobox/lead lines 165-170.
- Monongah mining disaster: staged `362 officially; estimates up to 500`; registered per-disaster article gives 362 killed, while a search for `500` found no match on the page. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monongah_mining_disaster, infobox/lead lines 119-125 and disaster section lines 131-142.

Minimal fix: either revise Death Toll cells to the registered per-disaster article wording under the current source-priority rule, or explicitly register a different value source for contested death-toll variants and update `source_urls`, `source_count`, roles, source-priority prose, and universe_listing notes accordingly.

2. (factual, BLOCKING) Several Primary Cause cells are not source-faithful under the same per-disaster value-source rule.

The causal column is load-bearing for this instance, so normalized cause text must be tightly grounded to infobox/lead/cause-section wording.

Representative mismatches:
- Coalbrook mining disaster: staged `Rock fall and collapse`; registered per-disaster article infobox says cascading pillar failure, and the cause section explains the cascading pillar-collapse mechanism. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coalbrook_mining_disaster, infobox lines 126-133 and cause section lines 168-171.
- Monongah mining disaster: staged `Mine explosion`; registered article infobox classifies the cause generically as a coal mine disaster, while the body says no official cause was determined and presents theories involving a spark igniting coal dust or methane. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monongah_mining_disaster, infobox lines 119-125 and disaster section lines 131-133.
- Banqiao Dam failure: staged `Typhoon Nina extreme rainfall overwhelming dam`; registered article infobox gives a multi-factor cause including Typhoon Nina, engineering flaws, and policy failures. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_Banqiao_Dam_failure, infobox lines 137-140 and background lines 152-155.
- Senghenydd: staged `Methane explosion`; registered article gives a more qualified account: the 1913 cause is described as unknown, with a later inquiry favoring a spark igniting firedamp. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senghenydd_colliery_disaster, lead lines 121-124.

Minimal fix: normalize each Primary Cause cell to the per-disaster article’s infobox/lead/cause-section phrasing, preserving uncertainty where the article states it. Add per-row notes if a concise normalized cause is deliberately shorter than the source phrase.

3. (structural, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE) Disaster-name normalization prose overclaims verbatim article-title use.

`curation.json::normalization_decisions[Disaster]` says Disaster values are verbatim from per-disaster article titles or disambiguated forms. That is not consistently true: `Senghenydd Colliery Disaster` differs from the current page title capitalization (`Senghenydd colliery disaster`); `Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster` redirects to `Fukushima nuclear accident`; and `Benxihu Colliery disaster` is intentionally an event label for the `Benxihu Colliery` article. The identities are clear, so this is not blocking.

Minimal fix: reword the normalization rule to say Disaster values are stable event labels drawn from the master/per-disaster page, with explicit title/redirect exceptions for Benxihu, Fukushima, and Senghenydd.

- Master structure exists and supports the broad industrial-disaster universe: `List of industrial disasters` is a narrative, cross-industry list with the expected sectioned structure. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_industrial_disasters.
- Wiki-family discovery found specialized sibling pages/lists for mining, nuclear/radiation, and disaster subdomains, but no single more direct Wikipedia source that displaces the selected cross-industry master for this partially_supplemented design.
